exposure: Pre-pregnancy BMI class (Class I: 30.0-34.9 kg/m2, Class II: 35-39.9 kg/m2, Class III: >=40 kg/m2)
Gestational weight gain (<11 pounds, 11-20 pounds, >20 pounds)
cohort: The study included 641 singleton pregnancies with a pre-pregnancy BMI >=30 kg/m2 who received care at an inner-city institution between January 1, 2016, and December 31, 2021.
finding: Higher pre-pregnancy BMI Class III was associated with increased maternal readmission within 6 weeks postpartum, and greater gestational weight gain was associated with increased rates of cesarean delivery, higher quantitative blood loss, longer length of hospitalization, and higher birthweights.
mod_finding: Greater gestational weight gain was associated with increased rates of cesarean delivery.
